summary: This memo extends the ForCES model of RFC 5812 and updates it to allow complex data types for metadata, optional default values and optional access types. It also fixes an LFB inheritance issue and adds an event condition and LFB properties.

eli5.summary: This RFC improves the description language that router designers use, adding more kinds of data and a few new features.

questions: what is the forces model extension
subtitle: Updates to the ForCES model schema: richer metadata, defaults, finer access control, a new event and LFB properties.

tldr.problem: After several years of use, the ForCES forwarding element model in RFC 5812 turned out to be missing modeling features, such as complex metadata, default values inside structures and per-component access types.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC extends the XML schema for LFB class libraries. It allows structs and arrays as metadata, adds optional default values and access types, adds the eventBecomesEqualTo event condition, defines LFB properties, adds a version attribute to derivedFrom and tightens validation.
tldr.outcome: The changes do not alter the ForCES protocol and stay backward compatible with libraries written under the old schema, but they use a new XML namespace, version 1.1.

today: RFC 7408 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5812. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the ForCES Model Needed an Update
sections.content:
The ForCES model in RFC 5812 defines Forwarding Element (FE) Logical Functional Blocks (LFBs) in XML. Experience with it showed a need for new modeling concepts and changes to existing ones, so RFC 7408 updates the model.

The changes are limited to the schema definition and need no change to the ForCES protocol in RFC 5810. Libraries written under the earlier schema are still valid under the new one. In the other direction, XML libraries produced with the new schema MUST NOT include any of the new features if they are to be compatible with existing ForCES implementations.

Extended parts of the schema are marked with the tags <!-- Extension RFC 7408 --> and <!-- /Extension RFC 7408 -->.
sections.eli5: The old form for describing router parts was missing a few boxes. This RFC adds them, and old filled-in forms still work.

sections.title: Complex Metadata, Defaults and Access Types
sections.content:
Complex metadata. The original schema allowed only atomic types (or a type reference) for metadata. The extension also allows array and struct, with key declarations that check array content keys and struct component IDs. The motivating cases come from the OpenFlow Switch Specification: an Action Set that travels with the packet, and a list of actions that accompanies a packet received from a controller.

Default values. A data type definition can now carry an optional defaultValue, so a type such as a counter that starts at 0 does not have to be respecified everywhere. The rules say that defaults MUST be ignored for non-atomic, non-base types, that a referencing type's default overrides the referenced one, that an LFB component's default overrides the data type's default, and that defaults on types referenced in capabilities or metadata MUST be ignored.

Access types. A struct component can now have its own access attribute (default read-write). It MUST override the access type of the enclosing struct, so a read-only counter can sit inside a read-write struct. Access types given for a component in a capability, or for a struct in metadata, MUST be ignored.
sections.eli5: Now a box on the form can say what number it starts with, and one box inside a bigger group can be marked look-but-do-not-touch even if the group is changeable.

sections.title: The eventBecomesEqualTo Event
sections.content:
The model gains a new event condition, eventBecomesEqualTo. Unlike eventGreaterThan and eventLessThan, it triggers when the value is exactly the threshold. It is useful for watching states: in the high availability design of RFC 7121, a master control element may want to know when a backup control element has just become associated.

The event MUST be triggered only when the target component's value becomes equal to the condition value, and implementations MUST NOT generate further events while the value stays equal.

To learn when the state later changes, a second eventChanged event can be defined, or eventBecomesEqualTo can be reused with eventHysteresis. For this condition, after the last notification a new one MUST be generated only once the value has changed by +/- V, where V is the hysteresis value. A control element developer should consider count or time filtering to avoid being overrun by messages.
sections.eli5: It is like an alarm that rings only at the moment a number hits exactly the number you picked, and does not keep ringing while the number stays there.

sections.title: LFB Properties
sections.content:
Components already had properties, but there was no way to see per-LFB-instance statistics, which are useful at least for debugging communication between a control element (CE) and a forwarding element. These properties are read-only.

To avoid ambiguity in protocol paths, LFB componentID 0 MUST refer to LFB properties, and ID 0 MUST NOT be used for any component definition. This is backward compatible because no known LFB definition uses componentID 0. The schema enforces it with a minExclusive value of 0.

The RFC defines an LFBProperties struct with eight uint32 components: packets, error packets and bytes sent to the CE, and the same four counters for what is received from the CE.
sections.eli5: Every building block now gets a little scoreboard at slot zero that counts the messages it sent and received, and how many had errors.

sections.title: Inheritance Fix, Validation and Compatibility
sections.content:
Inheritance. RFC 5812 let an LFB class inherit from another, but the schema named only the parent class. That was ambiguous when several versions of the parent exist. The derivedFrom element now takes an optional version attribute, for example <derivedFrom version='1.0'>EtherPHYCop</derivedFrom>. If it is omitted, derivedFrom means the first version of the parent, usually 1.0.

Validation. The schema adds uniqueness rules that did not exist before: metadataIDs, LFBClassIDs, componentIDs, capabilityIDs and event baseIDs per LFB, eventIDs per LFB, and special values per atomic data type. These checks work only within a single XML file.

Namespace. The schema namespace changes from 1.0 to 1.1. Definitions valid under the old namespace remain valid under the new one, but tools that process both will need to understand both.
sections.eli5: When a new block says it is built from an older one, it can now say which edition of the older one. The form also double-checks that no two things share the same ID number.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content:
IANA registered a new XML namespace, urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:forces:lfbmodel:1.1, with the IESG as registrant contact.

The RFC states that the additions do not change the nature of the initial model, so the security considerations of RFC 5812 apply as well, and the changes have no effect on the security semantics of the protocol. On pervasive monitoring, it says the new metadata might make monitoring slightly more elegant for an attacker who controls the LFBs, but does not enable new ways to abuse LFBs for it. Because the document specifies no protocol, protecting against passive eavesdropping is out of scope.
sections.eli5: The new boxes do not open any new doors for troublemakers, so the old safety rules still apply.

viz.caption: WHAT RFC 7408 ADDS TO THE FORCES MODEL

items.title: Complex metadata
items.text: Structs and arrays may be used as metadata.

items.title: Default values
items.text: Data type definitions can carry a defaultValue.

items.title: Struct access types
items.text: Each struct component can have its own access attribute.

items.title: eventBecomesEqualTo
items.text: An event that fires when a value becomes exactly the threshold.

items.title: Versioned derivedFrom
items.text: Optional version attribute on LFB class inheritance.
